newsitem.title: USA: Dollar falls in U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls in U.S. trade.

text.p: The dollar firmed overseas but weakened in U.S. trading Thursday after a mixed performance by the German mark in Europe sapped enthusiasm for the U.S. currency.

The mark rose to a seven-week high vs. the French franc despite a joint Franco-German effort to stamp out fears of a franc devaluation sparked by recent remarks by former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing.
But the mark fell to a 31-month low against the British pound and also slid to its lowest level against the Italian lira in a month.
"There is a lot of uncertainty in Europe ... that is really preventing the dollar from taking its own direction (against the mark)," said Kisoo Park, a senior trader at Bank of Boston.
On Thursday, the dollar stood at 111.27 Japanese yen, down from 111.55 yen at Wednesday's close, and at 1.4980 marks, up from 1.4965 late on Wednesday.

Giscard d'Estaing was quoted Wednesday in the weekly magazine l'Express as calling for French franc depreciation before France joins the proposed European Economic and Monetary Union. A weaker franc might revive French growth by making French exports more attractive.
Although Giscard now wields little real political power, his remarks carry weight because he was a founding father of plans for a single European currency along with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
The French government is deeply unpopular, and people are quick to blame the budget-slashing required for participating in a single currency for weak growth and mass unemployment.
The mark's rise against the franc indirectly helped weaken the dollar against the mark in U.S. trade.

However, in an effort at damage control Thursday, Kohl and French Prime Minister Alain Juppe issued a statement implicitly rejecting Giscard's questioning of France's "stubborn" determination to keep the franc tied to the mark.
"More recently, Giscard seems to have retracted (his statement) ... after a 75-minute conversation with Helmut kohl," said David Gilmore, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
The pound rose to a fresh four-year high against the dollar, ending at $1.6890, up from $1.6820 Wednesday.
The dollar edged up to 1.2665 Swiss francs from 1.2662 Swiss on Wednesday. It ended at Canadian $1.3395 vs. C$1.3396.
